idiom_name: module of pure functions; typing.Protocol for collaborators, a class only when several operations share one dependency set
implementation_notes: The lightest realization is a domain/services.py module of functions taking domain objects plus collaborators as keyword-only arguments: a function cannot accumulate instance state, which is the pattern's core requirement, so the service class of the classic structure is simply not needed. When several operations share the same collaborators, use a class or functools.partial whose construction takes them, and type the collaborators with typing.Protocol so the domain never imports infrastructure (runtime_checkable only if isinstance checks are genuinely needed). functools.singledispatch covers operations whose behaviour depends on the concrete type of a domain argument.
pitfalls: Module-level caches and globals are Python's version of service state (_rate_cache: dict = {}); they make behaviour depend on call history and are unsafe across threads.
Mutable default arguments (def convert(amount, target, cache={})) create hidden shared state between calls - the most common accidental stateful service in Python.
Protocols are checked by type checkers only: a collaborator with a slightly wrong signature fails at the call site unless tests or a checker cover the contract.
